blocks.text: Managing tab sprawl for SEO tasks

SEO work involves dozens of open tabs. You might have Google Search Console, an Ahrefs dashboard, and a client audit open at once. This creates noise. Use Chrome profiles to group these. Go to the profile icon in the top right, then click Add. Label them by client or project. This keeps your cookies and extensions separate. It also stops you from accidentally logging into the wrong account.

Technical audits require more than just a browser. You likely use Screaming Frog or Sitebulb. These are desktop apps. They do not live in Chrome. When you find an issue in your crawler, you often need to verify it in the browser. Use ⌘ ⇥ to switch between your audit tool and Chrome. Ask Lazur to point at specific settings if you get lost in complex menus.

Research is the bulk of your day. You read long pages and look for keyword opportunities. Instead of scrolling and reading every line, hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur to summarize the page. It reads the screen and gives you the key points. This saves you from reading irrelevant content. You can also ask it to explain a complex technical error you see on a page.

blocks.text: Reporting is manual. You copy data from Google Sheets into emails. Stop doing this by hand. Create templates in your email app. Use Lazur to dictate the text while you look at the data in Chrome. It ensures your tone is professional. You can also ask Lazur to guide you through complex Google Sheets formulas if you need to merge cells or count unique values.
Common mistakes in SEO browser workflows

The biggest mistake is mixing personal and work browsing. This messes up your search history and recommendations. Always use a dedicated work profile. Another mistake is keeping too many extensions active. They slow down your Mac and Chrome. Disable extensions you do not use daily. Check your extension manager often. If a page loads slowly, it is usually an extension conflict.

Interruptions kill your audit progress. It takes 23 minutes to refocus after a distraction. Use Chrome to block notifications from sites that do not matter. Go to Settings > Privacy and security > Site settings > Notifications. Remove sites that send you alerts. Keep your environment clean. Lazur can help here by setting quick timers for deep work sessions.

faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or operate apps. It points at things and guides you through steps so you can do the work yourself.

faq.question: Does Lazur work on older Macs?
faq.answer: Lazur works on macOS systems that support current app versions. Check the system requirements for your specific macOS version.

faq.question: How do I manage tab sprawl efficiently?
faq.answer: Use Chrome profiles to separate clients. Group related tabs and close what you are not using to keep your memory usage low.
